extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and patent agents (practitioners before the Canadian Patent Office/CIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Official CIPO practice guidance on filing, receipt dates, time limits, extensions, missing/erroneous communications, and filing-date / description requirements for Canadian patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for allegations of missing communications from the Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person alleges they did not receive a communication sent by the Office, they may submit an affidavit or statutory declaration containing information about their record keeping systems and copies of relevant records (e.g. mailroom or email docketing records) to demonstrate non-receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If upon review the Office is satisfied the communication was not received at the postal or email address, the Office will withdraw the communication and issue it again with a new date; if not satisfied, the Office informs the person by letter and will consider the communication received. If internal Office error/delay with the address on file is found, the Office will withdraw and reissue with a new due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for Erroneous Communications from the Patent Office or the Commissioner of Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where technical errors result in inadvertent sending of Notices for actions that are not or no longer prescribed, the Office will notify the recipient that such notices will be considered never sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any effects produced by those erroneous notices will be considered never to have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for allegations of missing communications from an external client to the Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant/patentee alleges a written communication was sent but not received by the Office, they must submit an affidavit or statutory declaration with documentary evidence that supports the allegation that an item was received by the Office on a specified day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence may include any indication of reception/transmission or payment receipt. Re-submission of the documents will also be required. If the Office is satisfied, the communication will be deemed received on the date supported by evidence; if not satisfied, it will be considered not received. If missing communications caused abandonment/expiry, the applicant may consider reinstatement under subsection 73(3) or reversal under subsection 46(5) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for allegations of delayed receipt of examiner’s report
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner’s report is alleged received more than one month after its date, the applicant may request withdrawal if, in addition to the requisition under subsection 86(2) or 86(5), it contains a requisition/requirement under section 85, 85.1 or 94 and an affidavit/statutory declaration with evidence is submitted within 14 days of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/statutory declaration must contain information about the person’s record keeping systems and copies of relevant records to demonstrate receipt > one month after report date. If satisfied, the Office will withdraw and issue a new report; if not, it will consider the report timely. Applicant may instead request an extension of time under subsection 3(1); the fee for such extension may be waived in certain circumstances (see referenced sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception – written communications sent before suspension, revocation or surrender of patent agent licence
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent agent’s licence is suspended, revoked or surrendered, the appointment of that agent is revoked; any written communication sent to that agent on the day of or within the four-month period preceding the suspension/revocation/surrender that has not been responded to is considered not to have been sent (section 11 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice the applicant is advised of the revocation and any written communications requiring action sent in the preceding four months will be reissued with a new due date and sent to the applicant. Applicant may also receive a notice requiring an appointment of agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt – physical delivery to Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt for physical delivery to the Patent Office depends on whether the Office is open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delivered when the Office is open to the public they are deemed received that day; if delivered when the Office is closed, they are deemed received on the first day the Office is next open (subsection 10(2) of the Patent Rules). See section 2.02.05a for means of physical delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt – physical delivery to designated establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt for physical delivery to designated establishments depends on whether the Office and the designated establishment are open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: if delivered to designated establishment when it is open and the Office is open, deemed received that day; if Office closed but designated establishment open, deemed received next Office-open day; if designated establishment closed when delivered, deemed received on first day the Office is next open to the public that falls on or after the day the designated establishment is next open (subsection 10(3)). See sections 2.02.05b and 2.02.05c for delivery methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt – submission by electronic means
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt for documents submitted by electronic means specified by the Commissioner is the day, according to the local time of the Patent Office, that they are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of whether the Office is open to the public or not. See section 2.02.07 for electronic submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When an action is required within a fixed number of months after a specified day, the time limit is calculated by: counting forward the number of months without including the month in which the day falls; excluding the specified day; and including in the last month the calendar day that has the same date as the specified day (or if none, the last day of that month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several illustrative examples are provided (e.g., examiner’s requisition dated Jan 15 with four-month response due May 15; maintenance-fee notice examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed days (subsection 78(1) extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed days for subsection 78(1) (days on which time periods ending on those days are extended) are enumerated and include weekends, statutory holidays and days the Office is closed to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full list copied from section 5 of the Patent Rules (Saturday, Sunday, Jan 1, Good Friday, Easter Monday, Monday before May 25, June 24 rules, July 1 rules, first Monday in August, first Monday in September, Sept 30 rules, second Monday in October, Nov 11 rules, Dec 25/26 rules, and any day on which the Patent Office is closed to the public). Example demonstrates how a notice of allowance due Nov 11 is extended depending on weekday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected closures of the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Unforeseen circumstances leading to unexpected closures (all or part of a day) will be announced and are treated under paragraph 5(n) as prescribed days for the purpose of subsection 78(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a time period ends on a day of unexpected closure, the time period is extended to the next day the Patent Office is open to the public. Section 78 does not apply to international applications during the international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated days – Commissioner discretion (force majeure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 78(2) the Commissioner may designate any day on account of unforeseen circumstances where it is in the public interest to extend time periods ending on that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation will be published on the CIPO website and extended to the next day the Office is open; this provision functions like a force majeure clause but is not so named in the Act/Rules. Section 78 does not apply to international phase applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extensions of time – subsection 3(1) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To request an extension under subsection 3(1) applicants/patentees must, prior to expiry of the time limit: submit a request from the default correspondent; pay the prescribed fee; and provide a justification of circumstances that satisfies the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of any requirement will result in refusal. Office offers no specific guidelines on justification content but will consider reasonable and detailed explanations. Commissioner will assess and may grant an extension at their discretion; applicant/patentee will be notified. Examples of eligible actions include extending response time to examiner’s requisition (to max six months) and response to Commissioner’s notice under section 65. Subsequent requests may be considered if time permits. Examples of exceptional circumstances that may justify further extension are provided (recent change in patent agent, severe illness, death, bankruptcy, other serious unforeseen circumstances). See section 2.03.03f for exceptions where subsection 3(1) does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time for Examiner Requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The time to respond to an examiner’s requisition is four months; the Commissioner may extend that time to a maximum of six months from the date of the examiner’s requisition under subsection 131(2) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once granted, the newly established due date is six months from the examiner’s requisition. Extension is not calculated by appending two months to a deemed expiry that fell on a designated/prescribed date. Any extension for an examiner’s requisition will not apply to any requirement to request continued examination that might form part of an examiner’s report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time – Delayed Receipt of Examiner Requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s requisition under 86(2) or 86(5) was received more than one month after it was sent, applicant may apply for extension within 14 days after receipt and must provide evidence satisfactory to the Commissioner of the date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfactory evidence includes official incoming correspondence reports, date-stamped copies, or other data showing date of receipt. If provided, the Commissioner will waive the prescribed fee to apply for the extension. If satisfied, the new due date will be four months from the day the requisition was received. Requests for extension beyond 4 months from date of receipt will be considered based on circumstances; fees for such further requests will not be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application of subsection 3(1) (list of fixed time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a specified list of actions for which the Commissioner cannot grant an extension under subsection 3(1) of the Patent Rules (i.e., time limits that are fixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document lists many specific sections (e.g., s15(4), s44(1), s67(1)/(2), s68(1)/(2), s72, s73(1), s77(1), s80(1), s81(1), s83(1), s85.1(3/4), s86(1/1.1/6/10/12), s87(1), s89(1)(b), s93(1), s95(1), ss104–109/112/116/130/133/135/154 etc.). Note: time limits fixed under the Patent Act cannot be extended under subsection 3(1); the period fixed by subsection 18(2) of the Patent Act is extendable under section 4 of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time to 'top-up' small entity fees – subsection 3(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may extend time for payment of fees paid at the small entity rate after expiry if the Commissioner considers circumstances justify and the following are met: (1) small entity fee was paid before expiry; (2) later determined standard fee should have been paid; (3) applicant/patentee files statement that fee was paid in good faith and request filed without undue delay after becoming aware; (4) pays difference between small entity and standard fee; and (5) pays extension of time fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant will be notified of decision. Lists fees eligible for 'top-up' (application fee, various maintenance fees, request for examination fee, continued examination fee, final fees, national phase fees, etc.). If compliant, 'top-up' payments are considered to have been made on date of original small entity fee (subsection 3(5)). Single request can cover multiple fees so long as extension fee and differences are paid for each. Patent Rules do not allow topping up of an application fee paid prior to Oct 30, 2019. If not all fees topped up, entity size remains small in Office records for future notices; difference remains on file and available for refund within three years upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time to 'top-up' request for examination fee – subsection 3(3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may allow extension after the end of time limit to request examination where an insufficient amount was paid for the examination fee (subject to exclusions) provided: the Office acknowledged the request was made within the prescribed time; it was later determined payment was insufficient; applicant files a statement that the extension is filed without undue delay and that underpayment was unintentional; and the applicant pays the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Office determines the request is compliant, the 'top-up' payment is considered to have been made on the date of the original insufficient payment (subsection 3(5)). See 11.01.02 for time to request examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time to 'top-up' – erroneous information – subsection 3(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commissioner provided erroneous information in writing concerning the amount of a fee (excluding information in Schedule 2), and the applicant paid an insufficient amount as a result, the Commissioner may extend time if the applicant: identifies the source of erroneous information; files a statement that the application is filed without undue delay after awareness; and pays the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements are met, the 'top-up' payment is considered made on the date of original insufficient payment (subsection 3(5)). Where applicable, the Office will reverse any consequence that occurred due to the insufficient fee being paid before the expiry of the period to pay the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limits for PCT national phase applications before national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 78 of the Patent Act (prescribed/designated day extensions) does not apply to international applications during the international phase; section 160 of the Patent Rules makes section 78 not apply to PCT national phase applications in respect of a time period that ended before national phase entry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For extensions during the international phase see MOPOP Section 34.08. Consult relevant PCT/national-phase provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three types of patent applications: Regular Canadian Patent Application (filed in Canada under the Patent Act), PCT National Phase Application (filed under the PCT later entering national phase in Canada under the Patent Rules), and Divisional Application (separation of a distinct invention from an original application into a distinct application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Chapter details documents and information required to secure filing dates for each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to obtain a filing date for a regular Canadian patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: To secure a filing date under subsection 28(1) of the Patent Act an applicant must provide the documents and information prescribed by section 71 of the Patent Rules: an indication that the elements submitted are intended to be an application for a patent; information allowing the applicant to be identified; information allowing the applicant to be contacted; and a document, in any language, that on the face of it appears to be a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prescribed documents/information are submitted on different dates, the filing date will be the latest of those dates. Submitting an application fee is not required to secure a filing date; if not submitted the Commissioner will send a notice requiring payment of the application fee and late fee within three months of the notice; failure to pay then leads to application being considered withdrawn under subsection 66(2) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide all information/documents to secure a filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required documents/information is missing, the applicant will be notified under subsection 28(2) and required to submit outstanding items within two months of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supplied within two months, the filing date is the date the last required document/information was submitted. If not supplied within two months, the application will be deemed to never have been filed pursuant to subsection 28(3) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description provided in a language other than English or French
rubrics_metrics.description: A description in a foreign language does not need to be in English/French to establish a filing date, but if a foreign language description is used to establish the filing date the applicant must submit an English or French translation of any part of the specification/drawings that was not entirely in English/French on the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is not submitted, the Commissioner will send a notice requiring submission within two months. If translation is submitted within two months, the translation will replace the original; failure to submit the translation within the prescribed time leads to abandonment under subsection 73(2) of the Patent Act as prescribed by subsection 132(1)(a) of the Patent Rules. See Chapter 9 for more on abandonment and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to a previously filed application in place of a description (subsection 27.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a reference statement to the Commissioner instead of the description to secure a filing date; the reference statement must be in English or French and state that a reference to a specified previously filed application is being submitted instead of all or part of the specification or drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prescribed period to make a complete reference statement begins on receipt of any document to establish a filing date and ends the earlier of two months from receipt (or other notice-based deadlines) or the filing date. A reference statement cannot be used to secure a filing date for a divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference statement content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference statement must include information about the previously filed application per paragraph 67(2)(a): the name of the country/office of filing and either the number of the previously filed application or, if not known, the provisional number and date with a copy of the request portion, or the applicant's reference number plus applicant name and postal address, title of the invention and date sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specifics are required so the Commissioner can identify the referenced filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the previously filed application (after submitting reference statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has two months from the date the reference statement was submitted to submit a copy of the previously filed application or make it available in a specified digital library and inform the Commissioner; if the previously filed application was filed in Canada, the applicant is exempted from providing a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant meets the requirements, the specification/drawings in the previously filed application are deemed by subsection 27.01(2) to have been contained in the application on the date the statement was received, and that will be the date of submission for the description. The filing date of the application will be the latest of the dates when the documents and information required under section 71 are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the previously filed application if not in English or French
rubrics_metrics.description: If all or part of the previously filed application is in a language other than English or French, the applicant must provide an English or French translation as required by subsection 15(2) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is not submitted when the copy is submitted, the Commissioner will send a notice under subsection 15(4) requiring translation submission within two months. If translation is submitted within two months it replaces the original; failure to submit within prescribed time leads to abandonment under subsection 73(2) of the Patent Act (as prescribed by subsection 132(1)(a) of the Patent Rules).
